title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 34
paragraphs: By saying this he followed Melampus's example in his demand, if one may compare royal power with mere citizenship. For Melampus, when the women of Argos were seized by madness and the Argives tried to hire him to come from Pylos and cure their women, demanded as payment for himself half the royal power; and the Argives would not allow this and departed. But afterwards, when more of their women became mad, at last they accepted what Melampus had proposed and went to offer it to him. Then he, seeing they had changed their minds, raised his demand and said he would not do what they wanted unless they also gave his brother Bias a third share in the royal power. Driven into a corner, the Argives consented to this too.
